name: Macbeth
hook: Shakespeare's shortest tragedy: prophecy, a dagger, a ghost, and a wood that walks.

facts.label: Duncan
facts.statement: Macbeth kills King Duncan in 1040 and seizes the Scottish throne; the play turns the murder into Shakespeare's darkest tragedy.

facts.label: the Weird Sisters
facts.statement: Three witches, called the Weird Sisters, greet Macbeth with prophecies that he will be thane of Cawdor and then king.

facts.label: Banquo's ghost
facts.statement: Macbeth has Banquo killed, then sees his ghost at a banquet; the witches promised Banquo's children would be kings.

facts.label: Macduff
facts.statement: Macduff, Thane of Fife, kills Macbeth — he was "not of woman born", having been cut from his mother's womb.

facts.label: Birnam Wood
facts.statement: Birnam Wood moves against Dunsinane, fulfilling the prophecy that Macbeth is safe until the wood comes to him.

facts.label: the dagger
facts.statement: Macbeth's soliloquy asks, "Is this a dagger which I see before me?" — a vision pointing him toward murder that later titled a Star Trek episode.

facts.label: The Sound and the Fury
facts.statement: Act V's speech about life as "a tale told by an idiot" gave Faulkner the title of The Sound and the Fury.
